newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jan distillate imports down on high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jan distillate imports down on high stocks.

text.p: Japan's middle distillate imports fell sharply in January due to high stockpiles, traders said on Monday.

Japan imported 619,000 kilolitres (kl) of kerosene and 49,000 kl of gas oil in January, down 11.9 percent and 36.4 percent, respectively, from a year earlier, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said.
MITI also said kerosene stockpiles at end-January jumped by 30 percent from a year earlier.
The growth in kerosene inventories was attributed to a milder weather this winter as well as brisk domestic production, traders said.
The utilisation rate of Japanese oil refineries was at 89.3 percent in January, up from 88.6 percent in the same month a year ago, and up from 84.9 percent in December.
Domestic kerosene production for the month, as a result, hit a record high at 3.5 million kl.
Amid higher kerosene stocks, some refineries shifted production from kerosene to gas oil, raising gas oil stockpile levels at end-Jaunary by 25 percent on the year, traders said.
Japan's naphtha imports in January dropped 15 percent from December, reflecting ethylene production cuts by Japanese petrochemical firms.
Several major ethylene manufacturers in Japan have slashed ethylene output by up to 10 percent since last month in a bid to cool the bullish regional naphtha market.
January C-grade heavy fuel oil imports plummeted by 51.3 percent from a year earlier, and domestic sales were also down 13.3 percent.
Demand for C-grade heavy fuel oil slackened as thermal power plants are using more natural gas, widely regarded as clean energy, instead of crude oil and heavy fuel oil, a MITI official said.
